definition_zh: 不利的；有害的；反对的；相反的
definition_en: unfavorable to success or well-being, or opposed and contrary to something
core_image: 帆船正顺风前行，一股逆向的侧风突然把船身推离航线
scene: 登山队刚出发不久，山脊上就压来一片铅灰色的云。The climb was called off because of adverse weather.
sceneCN: 这里的 adverse 是「不利的」（第 1 个义项：对顺利与安全有害的）；句意为由于天气恶劣，攀登被取消。

pos.zh: 形容词：不利的；有害的；反对的；相反的

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不利地；有害地」
由同一词根构成，义为「逆境；不幸」
由拉丁语 adversarius 而来，义为「对手；敌手」
加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「对抗性的」

senses.title: Against one's interests
senses.definition: harmful to success, health, or well-being, or making a good result less likely
senses.definitionCN: 对成功、健康或福祉有害的，或使好结果更难出现的
senses.example: Heavy rain had an adverse effect on the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨对收成产生了不利影响。
senses.why: ad- means towards and vertere means to turn, so adversus is 'turned towards' in a hostile way: an adverse force has turned round to face you.
senses.whyCN: ad- 表示朝向，vertere 表示转，adversus 是「转过来对着」，即掉头冲着你来的力量，所以 adverse 指不利。

senses.title: Opposed in opinion
senses.definition: not in favour of a plan, proposal, or position, and acting or speaking against it
senses.definitionCN: 不赞成某项计划、提议或立场的，并加以反对的
senses.example: The board remained adverse to any rise in membership fees.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会仍然反对提高任何会员费。
senses.why: The same turning image moves from events to the will: when someone is adverse to a proposal, their attitude has swung round to face it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「转身」的意象从事件转到意志上：说一个人 adverse to 某提议，就是他的态度已转过来对着它。

intro.en: One Latin verb of turning grows into a word for whatever turns against us.
intro.cn: 一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，长成了指称「掉头与我们作对之物」的词。

items.en: vertere meant to turn, and it underlies a large family: versus, reverse, convert and vertigo all turn in some way.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，它支撑起一大族词：versus、reverse、convert 与 vertigo 都带「转」的意思。

items.en: ad 'towards' plus versum 'turned' gave adversum, a phrase meaning 'towards, facing', which could turn hostile.
items.cn: ad（向）加 versum（转过的）构成 adversum，本指「朝向、面对」，也可以带出敌对的意味。

items.en: As an adjective adversus meant 'opposite, contrary, hostile'; as a noun, an adversary was the person facing you.
items.cn: 作形容词时 adversus 意为「对面的、相反的、敌对的」；作名词时指「面对着你的人」，即敌手。

items.en: Old French passed the adjective into English in the sense of contrary fortune or opposing circumstance.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词传入英语，当时多指「相反遭际」或「对立情形」。

items.en: English records adverse from the fourteenth century; the modern phrase adverse effect dates from later technical writing.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪起记录 adverse；现代常用的 adverse effect 则来自较晚的专业文献。

items.en: Today the word is most at home before nouns such as effect, weather and reaction, marking whatever works against a good outcome.
items.cn: 今天它最常放在 effect、weather、reaction 这类名词前，标记一切与好结果作对的因素。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root of turning; the second collects common words for what works against us.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「转」的拉丁词根；第二组收几个表示「与人作对」的常用词。

entries.definition: a difficult or unlucky situation; misfortune
an opponent in an argument, contest, or conflict
in a way that harms or works against something
to turn away or prevent something bad; same turning root, other prefix
entries.definitionCN: 避免；转移；同词根但前缀不同

entries.definition: not likely to produce a good result; the plain opposite of favourable
entries.definitionCN: 不利的；不妙的；favourable 的反义词

entries.definition: causing damage, especially to health; more physical than adverse
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；尤指对健康造成损害，比 adverse 更具体

entries.definition: openly unfriendly or opposed; stronger in feeling than adverse
entries.definitionCN: 敌对的；敌意的；情绪比 adverse 更强烈

entries.definition: causing harm or damage; a formal synonym common in reports
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；造成损害的；报告体常用

normalIntro.en: Three real pieces carry the word: ad-, vertere and the adjective ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由三个真实部件构成：ad-、vertere 与形容词词尾。

normal.en: ad- is towards and vertere is to turn, so adverse is turned against you.
normal.cn: ad- 是「朝向」，vertere 是「转」，adverse 就是转过来对着你。

normal.en: The same root gives versus, reverse and convert, all words of turning.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 versus、reverse、convert，都是「转」的词。

normal.en: adverse effect is the commonest pairing in medical and business writing.
normal.cn: adverse effect 是医学与商业文本里最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Do not confuse adverse with averse; averse describes a person's dislike.
normal.cn: 别把 adverse 与 averse 混用，averse 说的是人「不喜欢」。

normal.en: Spell it with -verse, the same ending as reverse.
normal.cn: 拼写是 -verse，和 reverse 的结尾一样。

abstract.en: Picture a sail turning flat against the wind, and the boat losing speed.
abstract.cn: 想象帆面转过来迎着风，船立刻慢下来。

abstract.en: See a row of arrows all pointing at one small figure on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一排箭头全部指向一个很小的人影。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that keeps swinging shut in your face, however often you open it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，你每推开一次，它都朝你脸上关回来。

examples.en: The drug may cause adverse effects in older patients.
examples.cn: 这种药可能在老年患者身上引起不良反应。

examples.en: Farmers struggled through a season of adverse conditions.
examples.cn: 农民在整整一季的不利条件中艰难支撑。

examples.en: She remained adverse to the idea of moving abroad.
examples.cn: 她仍然反对搬到国外去的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德沃斯」——爱德沃斯一遇逆风就掉头，处处跟他作对。

root: 拉丁语 adversus 由 ad-「朝向」与 vertere「转」构成，本义是「转过来对着、敌对的」，经古法语进入英语后专指「不利的、相反的」。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses share one image of turning: circumstances turn against you, or a person's will turns against a proposal.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用一个「转身」的意象：要么环境掉头与你作对，要么人的意志掉头反对某项提议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sail swings round and faces the wind, and the boat loses way.
core.cn: 核心意象：帆面转过来迎风，船随即失去速度。

branches.en: weather that pushes a climb off its route
branches.cn: 把登山计划推离路线的天气

branches.en: a vote that swings against a proposal
branches.cn: 转而反对提案的表决

branches.en: a drug acting against the body it should help
branches.cn: 与身体作对的药物

branches.en: a fixed hostile stance in a debate
branches.cn: 辩论中固定的敌对立场

branches.en: one turning root, used for events and for attitudes
branches.cn: 同一个「转」的词根，既用于事件也用于态度

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin verb of turning, and ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀、一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，加上普通的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: vertere and adversus are recorded Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: vertere 与 adversus 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，只有更早的印欧词根属重构。

definition_zh: 广告（英式口语）；提及、注意到（正式动词）
definition_en: a notice that promotes something, or in formal use, to call attention to a point
core_image: 街角橱窗里一张手写的小告示，把路人的目光拉过去
scene: 地铁站的柱子上贴着一张招租的小纸片。She spotted an advert for a flat near the station.
sceneCN: 这里的 advert 是「广告」（第 1 个义项：宣传某物的告示）；句意是她在车站附近看到一则公寓招租广告。

pos.zh: 名词：广告（英式口语，advertisement 的缩略）
动词：提及；注意到（正式用法，常与 to 连用）

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根构成，义为「做广告；宣传」
加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告宣传」
加 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」

senses.title: A public notice promoting something
senses.definition: a short public notice, especially in British English, that promotes a product, service, or vacancy
senses.definitionCN: 尤用于英式英语的简短公开告示，用来推介商品、服务或招聘岗位
senses.example: He answered a job advert in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他应征了当地报纸上的一则招聘广告。
senses.why: advert is simply advertisement cut short, so it keeps the idea of turning public attention towards something for sale.
senses.whyCN: advert 就是 advertisement 截短而来，因此保留了「把公众注意力转向某样待售之物」的意思。

senses.title: To refer to or mention
senses.definition: to turn one's attention to something in speech or writing; a formal verb usually followed by to
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或写作中把注意力转向某事；正式动词，通常后接 to
senses.example: The report adverted to the shortage of skilled staff.
senses.exampleCN: 报告提到了熟练员工的短缺。
senses.why: The verb preserves the Latin sense of vertere, to turn: the speaker turns the listener's mind towards a topic.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词保留了拉丁语 vertere「转」的意思：说话者把听者的心思转向某个话题。

intro.en: A Latin verb of turning becomes first a French warning, then an English notice.
intro.cn: 一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，先变成法语的提醒，再变成英语的告示。

items.en: vertere, to turn, is the root behind versus, reverse and convert as well as this family.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，除这一族词外还支撑 versus、reverse 与 convert。

items.en: advertere combined ad 'to' with vertere 'turn', meaning to turn the mind towards something, hence to notice.
items.cn: advertere 由 ad（向）与 vertere（转）合成，指把心思转向某物，因此有「注意」之义。

items.en: Old French avertir meant to warn or inform, and its noun avertissement meant a warning or notice.
items.cn: 古法语 avertir 意为「警告、告知」，其名词 avertissement 指「警告、通知」。

items.en: English took the verb advert in the sense of turning attention to something; the noun advertisement followed.
items.cn: 英语先借入动词 advert，表示把注意力转向某事；名词 advertisement 随后出现。

items.en: In British speech advertisement was clipped to advert, while the full verb survives mainly in formal writing.
items.cn: 英式口语把 advertisement 截短为 advert；完整的动词则主要留在正式书面语里。

note.en: The first group is the advertising family; the second gathers words that mean a notice or a mention.
note.cn: 第一组是广告词族；第二组收表示「告示」或「提及」的词。

entries.definition: to promote goods or a vacancy publicly
the full noun for a public promotion
the business or activity of promoting things
to turn away or prevent; shares the turning root
entries.definitionCN: 避免；转移；共享「转」的词根

entries.definition: a sign or announcement giving information
a formal public statement about something

normalIntro.en: The word is advertisement with its tail cut off, built on a Latin verb of turning.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 advertisement 去掉尾巴，底层是一个表示「转」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: advert is advertisement shortened, so it means the same notice.
normal.cn: advert 是 advertisement 的缩短形式，指的仍是那则告示。

normal.en: The verb advert to means to turn attention to a point.
normal.cn: 动词 advert to 意为把注意力转向某一点。

normal.en: British speakers say advert where Americans say ad.
normal.cn: 英国人常说 advert，美国人常说 ad。

normal.en: A job advert sits in the classified pages of a newspaper.
normal.cn: job advert 出现在报纸的分类广告版面。

normal.en: The Latin root vertere, to turn, also hides in reverse and convert.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 vertere（转）也藏在 reverse 与 convert 里。

abstract.en: Picture a shopkeeper turning a handwritten card towards the passing crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象店主把一张手写卡片转向过路的人群。

abstract.en: See a finger turning a listener's face towards a detail on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指把听者的脸转向地图上的某个细节。

abstract.en: Imagine two uses of one motion: one sells a chair, the other points out a fact.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个转身动作的两种用途：一种卖椅子，一种指出事实。

examples.en: She put an advert in the window for her old bicycle.
examples.cn: 她在橱窗里贴了一则旧自行车出售广告。

examples.en: The magazine was full of full-page adverts.
examples.cn: 这本杂志里全是整版广告。

examples.en: He adverted to the delay only at the end of the meeting.
examples.cn: 直到会议结束他才提到延误的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德沃特」——爱得我特地贴张告示，把大家都叫来看。

root: 拉丁语 advertere「把心思转向」由 ad-「向」与 vertere「转」构成；经古法语 avertir「告知」进入英语，再由 advertisement 截短为 advert。

sensesIntro.en: Two uses of one turning motion: a notice turns the public towards goods, and a formal verb turns the mind towards a point.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「转」的动作有两种用法：告示把公众转向商品，正式动词把心思转向某个要点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handwritten card turned towards the crowd in a shop window.
core.cn: 核心意象：橱窗里一张手写卡片转向人群。

branches.en: a card in a window pointing at a flat to let
branches.cn: 橱窗里指向待租公寓的卡片

branches.en: a newspaper column of posts waiting to be filled
branches.cn: 报纸上待招岗位的专栏

branches.en: a speaker turning listeners towards a shortage
branches.cn: 发言者把听众引向某个短缺问题

branches.en: a report that touches a risk in one sentence
branches.cn: 用一句话点到风险的报告

branches.en: the same turn, once towards goods and once towards a topic
branches.cn: 同一个转身，一次朝向商品，一次朝向话题

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin verb of turning, and English endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀、一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，加上构成词族的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: advertere is recorded Latin; the French noun avertissement is the bridge into English.
latinIntro.cn: advertere 是有记录的拉丁词；法语名词 avertissement 是进入英语的桥梁。

items.meaning: result or means of an action

definition_zh: 为……做广告；宣传；登广告招聘；使引人注意
definition_en: to make a product, service, or event publicly known in order to attract buyers or attention
core_image: 立在十字路口的一块巨幅海报，把远处的人流一批批引向店门
scene: 面包房新开张，店主在门口挂起手绘的牌子。They advertised the opening on every lamp post in the street.
sceneCN: 这里的 advertise 是「做广告宣传」（第 1 个义项：向公众推介商品或活动）；句意是他们在街上每根灯柱上都宣传了开业消息。

pos.zh: 动词：为……做广告；宣传；登广告招聘；使引人注意

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
加 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告者」
加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告宣传」
截短形式，义为「广告」（英式口语）

senses.title: Promote goods or services
senses.definition: to tell the public about a product, service, or event in order to persuade them to buy or attend
senses.definitionCN: 向公众介绍商品、服务或活动，以劝其购买或参加
senses.example: The bakery advertised its opening with free bread.
senses.exampleCN: 面包房用免费面包来宣传开业。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to turn attention towards something; commerce turned that motion into paid publicity for goods.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本指把注意力转向某物；商业把这一动作变成了为商品付费的公开宣传。

senses.title: Announce a vacancy
senses.definition: to publish a notice that a job is available, usually with the preposition for
senses.definitionCN: 刊登某职位空缺的启事，通常与介词 for 连用
senses.example: The hospital is advertising for two nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院正在登广告招聘两名护士。
senses.why: A post that needs filling is treated like goods on offer: the same public notice is turned towards possible applicants.
senses.whyCN: 空缺的岗位被当作待售之物：同一种公开告示被转向潜在的应聘者。

senses.title: Make something conspicuous
senses.definition: to make a quality, fact, or oneself openly visible, sometimes with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 把某种品质、事实或自己公开显露出来，有时带贬义
senses.example: He never advertised his own successes.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不炫耀自己的成绩。
senses.why: If attention can be turned towards goods, it can also be turned towards a person or a virtue; the word then shades into showing off.
senses.whyCN: 注意力既能引向商品，也能引向某个人或某种美德；于是这个词就带上了炫耀的色彩。

intro.en: From a Latin verb of noticing to a verb of paid public promotion.
intro.cn: 从一个表示「注意到」的拉丁动词，走到一个表示「付费公开宣传」的动词。

items.en: vertere meant to turn and underlies versus, reverse, convert and this whole family.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，支撑 versus、reverse、convert 以及这一整族词。

items.en: advertere, from ad 'to' and vertere 'turn', meant to turn the mind towards a thing, hence to notice it.
items.cn: advertere 由 ad（向）与 vertere（转）构成，指把心思转向某物，因此有「注意」之义。

items.en: Old French avertir meant to warn or inform; its noun avertissement supplied the sense of a public notice.
items.cn: 古法语 avertir 意为「警告、告知」，其名词 avertissement 提供了「公开告示」的含义。

items.en: English first used advertise in the sense of drawing attention to something, without any commercial colour.
items.cn: 英语早期使用 advertise 时只表示「使人注意某事」，并不带商业色彩。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the commercial sense had taken over, and advertise came to mean promoting goods for sale.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，商业义占了上风，advertise 逐渐专指为出售的商品做宣传。

note.en: The first group shares the advertising root; the second gathers verbs of promoting and publicising.
note.cn: 第一组共享广告词根；第二组收表示「推广、宣传」的动词。

normal.cn: 词根 vertere（转）也出现在 reverse 与 convert 中。

abstract.en: Picture a huge poster turning the current of pedestrians towards one door.
abstract.cn: 想象一块巨幅海报把人流的方向转向一扇门。

abstract.en: See the same poster rehung at a hospital gate, now pointing at a job rather than a sale.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张海报挪到医院门口，指向的不再是促销而是岗位。

abstract.en: Imagine a man holding a mirror that turns every passer-by towards his own face.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人举着镜子，把每个路人都转向他自己的脸。

examples.en: They advertised the concert on local radio for a week.
examples.cn: 他们在当地电台为音乐会做了一周广告。

examples.en: The company is advertising for a new accountant.
examples.cn: 这家公司正在登广告招聘一名新会计。

examples.en: She advertised her skills without ever sounding boastful.
examples.cn: 她展示自己的本领，却从不显得自夸。

root: 拉丁语 advertere「把心思转向」由 ad-「向」与 vertere「转」构成；经古法语 avertir 进入英语，十五世纪作「使人注意」，十八世纪转为「为商品做广告」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses move from goods to vacancies to self-display, all driven by the same turning of public attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从商品到岗位再到自我展示，驱动它们的都是同一个「把公众注意力转过来」的动作。

branches.cn: 手机厂商买下的电视时段

branches.en: a man turning attention towards his own record
branches.cn: 把自己的成绩转向众人目光的人

branches.cn: 同一个「转」的动词，可指向商品、岗位或自己

intro.en: A Latin verb of turning plus English verb and noun endings.
intro.cn: 一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，加上英语的动词与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: advertere is recorded Latin; the commercial sense developed only in English.
latinIntro.cn: advertere 是有记录的拉丁词；商业义项是英语里才发展出来的。

items.meaning: result or means of an action

definition_zh: 广告；（广告）宣传；体现……的典型例子
definition_en: a public notice or short film that promotes a product or service, or the activity of promoting something publicly
core_image: 地铁车厢里一整排灯箱，每一格都在向乘客推荐一样东西
scene: 电影开场前的黑暗里，银幕忽然亮起一段三十秒的推销短片。The advertisement for the new phone ran before every film.
sceneCN: 这里的 advertisement 是「广告」（第 1 个义项：宣传商品或服务的公开短片或告示）；句意是新手机的广告在每场电影前播放。

pos.zh: 名词：广告；广告宣传；体现……的典型例子

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ment 还原为动词，义为「做广告；宣传」
加 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告者」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告宣传」
截短形式，义为「广告」（英式口语）

senses.title: A public notice or film
senses.definition: a notice, picture, or short film that promotes a product, service, or event
senses.definitionCN: 推介商品、服务或活动的告示、图片或短片
senses.example: The advertisement for the new phone ran before every film.
senses.exampleCN: 新手机的广告在每场电影前播放。
senses.why: The noun names the finished object produced by the act of advertising, so it is the poster or film itself that turns attention to goods.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指「做广告」这一动作产出的成品，所以它是一张海报或一段短片，把注意力引向商品。

senses.title: The business of promoting
senses.definition: the activity of promoting goods, services, or posts publicly, used as an uncountable noun
senses.definitionCN: 公开推介商品、服务或岗位的活动，作不可数名词使用
senses.example: Advertisement is expensive for a small shop with a narrow margin.
senses.exampleCN: 对利润微薄的小店来说，做广告很昂贵。
senses.why: The same noun can name the activity rather than a single notice, especially in formal or business writing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可以指整项活动，而不是某一则告示，尤其在正式或商业文本中。

senses.title: A conspicuous example
senses.definition: a person or thing so good that it seems to recommend whatever it belongs to
senses.definitionCN: 好到仿佛在替所属之物做推荐的人或事物
senses.example: Her calm manner is an advertisement for the school's training.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉着的举止就是这所学校培养成果的活招牌。
senses.why: A good advertisement makes people want the product; by extension a fine example makes people want whatever produced it.
senses.whyCN: 好广告让人想要那件商品；引申开来，出色的范例也让人想要造就它的那套东西。

intro.en: The noun of a Latin turning verb, reshaped in French and then in English commerce.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁「转」动词的名词形式，经法语改造后进入英国商业。

items.en: vertere, to turn, is the root of versus, reverse, convert and this family.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，是 versus、reverse、convert 及其同族词的根。

items.en: advertere meant to turn the mind towards something, hence to notice or heed it.
items.cn: advertere 指把心思转向某物，因此有「注意、留心」之意。

items.en: Old French avertissement meant a warning or a piece of information made public.
items.cn: 古法语 avertissement 指「警告」或向公众告知的消息。

items.en: English formed advertisement as 'the act of drawing attention'; the modern commercial sense is later.
items.cn: 英语最初把 advertisement 用作「使人注意的行为」，现代的商业义出现得更晚。

items.en: Since the eighteenth century the word has meant a paid public promotion, and later also the trade that produces it.
items.cn: 十八世纪以后，这个词指付费的公开宣传，后来又指从事这一行当的行业。

note.en: The first group is the advertisement family; the second gathers other names for promotional notices.
note.cn: 第一组是 advertisement 词族；第二组收其他表示「宣传性告示」的词。

entries.definition: to promote goods publicly
the industry or activity of promoting
one who pays for advertisements
the short British word for an advertisement
a paid advertisement on television or radio
a sign or sheet giving public information
an activity intended to make a product more popular
a large printed picture used to advertise something

normalIntro.en: The noun adds -ment to the verb advertise; the root still means turning attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词由动词 advertise 加 -ment 构成，词根仍是「把注意力转过来」。

normal.en: advertise plus -ment gives the thing that results from advertising.
normal.cn: advertise 加 -ment，就是做广告之后得到的那件东西。

normal.en: The short British form is advert, and the American short form is ad.
normal.cn: 英式缩略是 advert，美式缩略是 ad。

normal.en: An advertisement for a job is a job advertisement.
normal.cn: 招聘岗位的广告就是 job advertisement。

normal.en: The -ment ending marks a result, as in movement and agreement.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ment 标记结果，如 movement 与 agreement。

normal.en: Spell the middle as -tise-, not -tize-, in British English.
normal.cn: 英式拼写中间是 -tise-，不是 -tize-。

abstract.en: Picture a row of lit boxes in a train, each one turning a passenger's eyes to a product.
abstract.cn: 想象车厢里一排发亮的灯箱，每一格都把乘客的目光转向一样商品。

abstract.en: See the same boxes counted not one by one but as an entire industry.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的灯箱不再逐个数，而是整体看作一个行业。

abstract.en: Imagine a well-dressed graduate who himself seems to recommend the school he came from.
abstract.cn: 想象一位衣着得体的毕业生，他本人就像在替母校做推荐。

examples.en: She answered an advertisement for a part-time cook.
examples.cn: 她应征了一则兼职厨师的广告。

examples.en: The walls were covered with advertisements for cheap flights.
examples.cn: 墙上贴满了廉价航班的广告。

examples.en: His tidy garden is an advertisement for patient work.
examples.cn: 他整洁的花园就是耐心劳作的活招牌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德沃泰斯门特」——爱得我太斯文，特地把广告贴满整条街。

root: 拉丁语 advertere「把心思转向」的名词形式，经古法语 avertissement 进入英语；-ment 表结果，本指「使人注意之物」，十八世纪起专指付费的商业广告。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses narrow from the finished notice to the whole trade, then widen again to any example that recommends what produced it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从一则成品告示，收到整个行业，再放宽到任何能替其来源做推荐的范例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of lit boxes, each turning a passenger's eyes towards one product.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排发亮的灯箱，每一格都把乘客的目光转向一样商品。

branches.en: a thirty-second film before a movie
branches.cn: 电影前三十秒的短片

branches.en: a full page in a magazine
branches.cn: 杂志里的整版页面

branches.en: the budget a small shop sets aside for publicity
branches.cn: 小店为宣传留出的预算

branches.en: a calm graduate who recommends his school
branches.cn: 沉着的毕业生替母校做推荐

branches.en: the notice, the trade, and the living example
branches.cn: 告示本身、整个行业与活的范例

intro.en: A Latin turning verb with the noun ending -ment, plus a cluster of English relatives.
intro.cn: 一个表示「转」的拉丁动词加名词词尾 -ment，再加一串英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: advertere is recorded Latin; the commercial narrowing happened in English.
latinIntro.cn: advertere 是有记录的拉丁词；商业义项的收窄发生在英语里。

items.meaning: result or means of an action

definition_zh: 建议；忠告；专业意见；（商业或外交上的）正式通知
definition_en: an opinion offered to help someone decide or act, or a formal business notice about a transaction
core_image: 朋友在岔路口伸手指向其中一条路，因为他已经替你看过前面
scene: 她把两份工作邀约摊在桌上，给老朋友打了电话。He asked his mentor for advice before signing the contract.
sceneCN: 这里的 advice 是「建议」（第 1 个义项：帮助他人决定或行动的意见）；句意是签约之前他向导师请教。

pos.zh: 名词：建议；忠告；专业意见；正式通知

derivatives.zh: 由同一词源构成，义为「建议；通知」
加 -er 构成，义为「顾问；提供建议者」
加 -ory 构成，义为「咨询的；劝告性的」
加 -able 构成，义为「明智的；可取的」

senses.title: An opinion to guide action
senses.definition: an opinion or suggestion offered to help someone choose what to do
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助他人决定该怎么做而提出的意见或提议
senses.example: He asked his mentor for advice before signing the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 签约之前他向导师请教。
senses.why: Old French avis came from Latin visum, 'what seems': advice is what seems best to the person who has looked at your situation.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 avis 来自拉丁语 visum「看上去的样子」：advice 就是看过你的处境之后，那人认为最好的做法。

senses.title: A formal business notice
senses.definition: an official notification about a transaction, shipment, or payment, usually in writing
senses.definitionCN: 关于交易、装运或付款的正式书面通知
senses.example: The bank sent an advice of the transfer to both accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 银行向两个账户都发送了转账通知。
senses.why: The same noun drifted from a private opinion to an official one: a notice tells the other party what it needs to know, just as advice tells a person what to do.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从私人意见漂移到官方意见：通知是告知对方该知道的事，正如建议是告知一个人该怎么做。

intro.en: A word about seeing and judging, borrowed through French and later split from advise.
intro.cn: 一个关于「看」与「判断」的词，经由法语借入，后来与 advise 分了家。

items.en: videre meant to see, and it underlies vision, video and evident as well as this family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，它支撑 vision、video、evident 以及这一族词。

items.en: The participle visum meant 'seen' and, as a noun, 'what seems or appears' to a person.
items.cn: 分词 visum 意为「被看到的」，作名词时指「在某人看来如此的东西」。

items.en: Old French avis meant an opinion or judgment, literally what appears good to the mind.
items.cn: 古法语 avis 意为「意见、判断」，字面是「在心思里显得好」。

items.en: Middle English adopted avis as advice and kept the -c- from the Latin spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语把 avis 借作 advice，并保留了拉丁拼写中的 -c-。

items.en: Spelling separated the noun advice from the verb advise; the noun also took on the official notice sense.
items.cn: 拼写把名词 advice 与动词 advise 分开；名词还发展出「正式通知」的义项。

note.en: The first group is the advice family with its -ice and -ise split; the second gathers words for guidance and formal notification.
note.cn: 第一组是 advice 词族，包含 -ice 与 -ise 的分工；第二组收表示「指导」与「正式告知」的词。

entries.definition: to give advice; the -ise spelling is the verb
a person whose job is to give advice
having the function of giving advice
sensible and worth doing
help and direction given by someone more experienced
formal advice, especially on serious personal or legal matters
a suggestion that something should be chosen or done
an official statement giving information

normalIntro.en: The noun and verb are twins: -ice for the thing given, -ise for the act of giving it.
normalIntro.cn: 名词与动词是一对双胞胎：-ice 指给出的东西，-ise 指给出这个动作。

normal.en: adVICE is the noun; adVISE is the verb, with the same hissing sound.
normal.cn: adVICE 是名词，adVISE 是动词，读音一样。

normal.en: You give advice, but you advise a person.
normal.cn: 你 give advice（给出建议），但你 advise 一个人（向某人提建议）。

normal.en: A piece of advice treats the noun as countable in small units.
normal.cn: a piece of advice 把不可数的 advice 拆成一条条来数。

normal.en: Old French avis came from Latin visum, what seems right.
normal.cn: 古法语 avis 来自拉丁语 visum，即「看上去合适的东西」。

normal.en: Legal advice and advice of payment use the same noun in two worlds.
normal.cn: legal advice 与 advice of payment 是同一个名词在两个世界里的用法。

abstract.en: Picture a friend standing at a fork, pointing down the road that looks clearer.
abstract.cn: 想象朋友站在岔路口，指着那条看起来更清楚的路。

abstract.en: See the same hand become an official clerk sliding a notice across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手变成柜员，把一张通知单从柜台推过来。

abstract.en: Imagine the difference between a spoken opinion and a stamped sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一句口头意见与一张盖章纸片之间的差别。

examples.en: She gave me some useful advice about the interview.
examples.cn: 她给了我一些关于面试的有用建议。

examples.en: On his advice, we waited another day before sailing.
examples.cn: 照他的忠告，我们又等了一天才出海。

examples.en: The advice note listed every item in the shipment.
examples.cn: 通知单上列明了这批货物的每一项。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德外斯」——爱得我特地跑到 wiser 的人面前，请他给条建议。

root: 古法语 avis「意见」来自拉丁语 visum「看来如此」，而 visum 又出于 videre「看」；中古英语借入作 advice，后来与动词 advise 在拼写上分工。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses grow from one idea of what seems right: a private opinion for action, and an official notice for information.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都长自「看来如此」这一个想法：私人的行动意见，与官方的信息通知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a friend at a fork pointing down the clearer road.
core.cn: 核心意象：朋友在岔路口指向更清楚的那条路。

branches.en: a mentor reading a contract before it is signed
branches.cn: 导师在签约前替你看合同

branches.en: a friend warning you about a difficult boss
branches.cn: 朋友提醒你某位上司难相处

branches.en: professional advice on a legal question
branches.cn: 就法律问题给出的专业意见

branches.en: a bank slip telling you a transfer has gone through
branches.cn: 告诉你转账已完成的银行通知单

branches.en: one word for what someone needs to know
branches.cn: 同一个词，指对方需要知道的事

intro.en: A Latin verb of seeing, a French noun of opinion, and English endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「看」的拉丁动词、一个表示「意见」的法语名词，加上构成词族的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: videre and visum are recorded Latin; avis is the Old French stage.
latinIntro.cn: videre 与 visum 是有记录的拉丁词；avis 是古法语阶段的形态。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被看到的；看来如此之物

definition_zh: 明智的；可取的；适宜的
definition_en: sensible and likely to bring a good result, and therefore worth doing or choosing
core_image: 山路入口竖着一块牌子，提示前方塌方、请走另一侧
scene: 天色转暗，向导抬头看了看压下来的云层。It is advisable to begin the descent before the storm arrives.
sceneCN: 这里的 advisable 是「明智的、可取的」（第 1 个义项：值得采取、能避免麻烦的）；句意是在暴风雨到来之前开始下撤是明智的。

pos.zh: 形容词：明智的；可取的；适宜的

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -able 还原为动词，义为「建议；劝告」
同源名词，义为「建议；忠告」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「顾问」
加 -ory 构成，义为「咨询的；劝告性的」

senses.title: Wise and worth doing
senses.definition: sensible because it is likely to produce a good result or avoid trouble
senses.definitionCN: 因为很可能带来好结果或避开麻烦而显得明智的
senses.example: It is advisable to begin the descent before the storm arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 在暴风雨到来之前开始下撤是明智的。
senses.why: The suffix -able makes the word mean 'able to be advised': an action that a sensible adviser would recommend is advisable.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 让这个词表示「值得被建议的」：一个明智的顾问会推荐的做法，就是 advisable。

senses.title: Suitable as a measure
senses.definition: described of a plan or measure that is judged proper and suitable in a formal context
senses.definitionCN: 正式语境中形容某项方案或措施被认为恰当、适宜
senses.example: The committee treated a full review as the advisable course.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会认为全面复查才是可取的做法。
senses.why: Placed before a noun, the word shifts from 'it would be wise to' to 'judged proper as a measure', which is how official reports use it.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前时，它从「这样做会明智」转为「作为措施被认为得当」，官方报告正是这样用的。

intro.en: An adjective formed in English from advise, which itself came from Latin through French.
intro.cn: 这是英语在动词 advise 上构成的形容词，而 advise 本身经由法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: videre, to see, gave visum, 'what seems', the base of the whole advice family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，其分词 visum 表示「看来如此之物」，是整族词的底子。

items.en: Medieval Latin advisare meant to consider or take counsel, built on the same 'seem' root.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 advisare 意为「考虑、商议」，同样建立在「看来如此」这个词根上。

items.en: Old French aviser meant to look at, consider, or give an opinion, and English borrowed it as advise.
items.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为「察看、考虑、给出意见」，英语借入后成为 advise。

items.en: English added -able to advise, first in the sense 'able to be advised', then 'worth advising'.
items.cn: 英语给 advise 加上 -able，先表示「可以被告知的」，后来转为「值得建议的」。

items.en: Today the word almost always appears in the frame it is advisable to do something, especially in guidance and rules.
items.cn: 今天它几乎总出现在「it is advisable to do something」这一句框里，多见于指南与规章。

note.en: The first group shares the advice root; the second gathers adjectives of prudence and suitability.
note.cn: 第一组共享 advice 词根；第二组收表示「审慎、适宜」的形容词。

entries.definition: to give advice or inform someone
an opinion offered to guide action
giving advice rather than making rules
in a way that is sensible; a rare adverb
entries.definitionCN: 明智地；罕见的副词形式

entries.definition: showing good judgment; broader than advisable
entries.definitionCN: 明智的；比 advisable 更宽泛

entries.definition: careful about the future and avoiding risk
entries.definitionCN: 审慎的；注重规避风险的

entries.definition: put forward as the thing to choose
fitting the situation; says nothing about wisdom
entries.definitionCN: 合适的；不涉及是否明智

normalIntro.en: The word is advise plus -able, so it names an action that deserves to be advised.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 advise 加 -able，指一种值得被建议采取的做法。

normal.en: advise plus -able gives 'worth advising', hence wise to do.
normal.cn: advise 加 -able 就是「值得被建议的」，因此是「明智的」。

normal.en: The usual frame is it is advisable to do something.
normal.cn: 最常见的句框是「it is advisable to do something」。

normal.en: Unlike advice, the adjective has no -ice spelling trap.
normal.cn: 与名词 advice 不同，这个形容词没有 -ice 的拼写陷阱。

normal.en: Highly advisable is the common intensifier in official guidance.
normal.cn: highly advisable 是官方指南里常见的加强说法。

normal.en: The root visum, what seems, also lies behind vision and evident.
normal.cn: 词根 visum（看来如此）也藏在 vision 与 evident 背后。

abstract.en: Picture a warning board at a trailhead pointing to the safer path.
abstract.cn: 想象登山口一块警示牌，指向更安全的那条路。

abstract.en: See a committee underlining one line of a report as the course to take.
abstract.cn: 想象委员会在报告里给一行字划线，标出该走的路线。

abstract.en: Imagine advice turned into an adjective, so the opinion becomes a property of the act.
abstract.cn: 想象建议变成一个形容词，意见于是成了那个动作本身的属性。

examples.en: It is advisable to book tickets well before the holiday.
examples.cn: 最好在假期前尽早订票。

examples.en: Regular checks are advisable for any old electrical wiring.
examples.cn: 任何老旧的电路都宜定期检查。

examples.en: The doctor thought a second opinion advisable.
examples.cn: 医生认为再听取一位医生的意见是明智的。

sensesIntro.en: One judgment of good sense appears twice: as a general verdict on an action, and as a formal label on a chosen measure.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「有道理」的判断出现两次：一次是对某动作的总体评断，一次是给某项措施贴上的正式标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warning board at a trailhead pointing to the safer path.

branches.en: starting down a mountain before the storm
branches.cn: 在暴风雨前开始下山

branches.en: booking early for a holiday
branches.cn: 假期前尽早订票

branches.en: a full review adopted as the proper measure
branches.cn: 被定为得当措施的全面复查

branches.en: an official report naming the course to take
branches.cn: 官方报告中点明该走的路线

branches.en: good sense, spoken as a verdict or written as a label
branches.cn: 同一个「有道理」，或说成评断，或写成标签

intro.en: The verb advise plus the adjective ending -able, with the same seeing root underneath.

latinIntro.en: visum and advisare are recorded forms; the -able adjective is a later English build.

definition_zh: 建议；劝告；（专业上）提供意见；正式通知
definition_en: to tell someone what you think they should do, to give professional guidance, or to inform someone formally
core_image: 一位老船长站在码头边，替年轻水手看风向、指航线
scene: 雨还没停，医生在诊室门口叫住了她。The doctor advised her to rest for a week.
sceneCN: 这里的 advise 是「建议、劝告」（第 1 个义项：告诉某人该怎么做）；句意是医生建议她休息一周。

pos.zh: 动词：建议；劝告；提供专业意见；正式通知

derivatives.zh: 同源名词，义为「建议；忠告」
加 -er 构成，义为「顾问；提供建议者」
加 -ory 构成，义为「咨询的；劝告性的」
加 -able 构成，义为「明智的；可取的」

senses.title: Tell someone what to do
senses.definition: to tell someone what you think is best for them to do, often with to or against
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人你认为他最好怎么做，常与 to 或 against 连用
senses.example: The doctor advised her to rest for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议她休息一周。
senses.why: Built on the same root as advice, the verb names the act of handing over that opinion instead of the opinion itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词与名词 advice 同源，指把那份意见交出去的动作，而不是意见本身。

senses.title: Give professional guidance
senses.definition: to act as an expert adviser on a matter, often for a fee or in an official role
senses.definitionCN: 作为专家就可提供意见，常为收费或担任公职
senses.example: She advises the government on energy policy.
senses.exampleCN: 她就能源政策向政府提供意见。
senses.why: When the adviser is a professional, the verb stops being friendly counsel and becomes a service delivered to a client.
senses.whyCN: 当提建议的人是专业人士时，这个动词就不再是朋友式的劝告，而成了向客户提供的服务。

senses.title: Inform someone formally
senses.definition: to give someone official information about a fact, decision, or change
senses.definitionCN: 把事实、决定或变动正式告知某人
senses.example: Please advise us of any change to your address.
senses.exampleCN: 地址如有变动，请通知我们。
senses.why: In commerce and law the verb keeps the older sense of making someone aware, without any element of recommending.
senses.whyCN: 在商业与法律语境里，这个动词保留了「使某人知晓」的旧义，完全不含推荐的意思。

intro.en: A verb of looking and judging, borrowed from French and later split by spelling from the noun.
intro.cn: 一个表示「看」与「判断」的动词，借自法语，后来在拼写上同名词分了家。

items.en: videre meant to see; its participle visum meant 'what seems', the seed of the whole family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，其分词 visum 表示「看来如此之物」，是整族词的种子。

items.en: Medieval Latin advisare meant to consider or take counsel, formed on the same seeming root.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 advisare 意为「考虑、商议」，建立在同一个词根上。

items.en: Old French aviser meant to look at, reflect on, or give an opinion about something.
items.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为「察看、思索或对某事给出意见」。

items.en: English borrowed advise with both the 'counsel' and the 'inform' senses already present.
items.cn: 英语借入 advise 时，「劝告」与「告知」两个义项已经并存。

items.en: Spelling settled advise for the verb and advice for the noun, though both sound the same.
items.cn: 拼写最终定下动词用 advise、名词用 advice，尽管两者读音相同。

note.en: The first group is the advice family; the second gathers verbs of recommending, guiding, and informing.
note.cn: 第一组是 advice 词族；第二组收表示「推荐、指导、告知」的动词。

entries.definition: the opinion that is given; the noun keeps -ice
entries.definitionCN: 被给出的意见；名词拼作 -ice

entries.definition: a person who advises
serving to give advice
sensible and worth doing
to say that something is good and should be chosen

entries.definitionCN: 正式劝告；提供专业意见

entries.definition: to put an idea forward for consideration, less forceful than advise
entries.definitionCN: 提议；语气比 advise 弱

entries.definition: to tell someone a fact officially

normalIntro.en: The verb ends in -ise, and its noun twin ends in -ice; both come from a root meaning 'what seems'.
normalIntro.cn: 动词以 -ise 结尾，名词双胞胎以 -ice 结尾；两者都来自「看来如此」这个词根。

normal.en: advise is the verb, advice is the noun, and the sound is the same.
normal.cn: advise 是动词，advice 是名词，两者读音相同。

normal.en: You advise someone to do something, or advise against it.
normal.cn: 你可以 advise someone to do something，也可以 advise against it。

normal.en: A professional advises a client on a specialist matter.
normal.cn: 专业人士就专门问题 advise 客户。

normal.en: Please advise us of changes is a standard line in business letters.
normal.cn: Please advise us of changes 是商务信函里的标准说法。

normal.en: The -ise ending tells you it is an action, not a thing.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ise 提示这是动作，不是一件东西。

abstract.en: Picture an old captain reading the wind and pointing a young sailor to the safer channel.
abstract.cn: 想象老船长看风，把年轻水手引向更安全的航道。

abstract.en: See the same captain now paid by a shipping company to write a route report.
abstract.cn: 想象同一位船长受航运公司聘请，写出一份航线报告。

abstract.en: Imagine a clerk simply handing over a sheet that says the address must be updated.
abstract.cn: 想象一名职员只递来一张纸，上面写着地址需要更新。

examples.en: The doctor advised her to rest for a week.
examples.cn: 医生建议她休息一周。

examples.en: Our lawyer advises clients on employment contracts.
examples.cn: 我们的律师就劳动合同向客户提供意见。

examples.en: Passengers are advised that the platform has changed.
examples.cn: 乘客已被告知站台变更。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德外兹」——爱得我特地跑去问兹事体大不大，请人给个建议。

root: 经古法语 aviser 上溯中世纪拉丁语 advisare，再往前是拉丁语 videre「看」及其分词 visum「看来如此之物」；英语借入时已含「劝告」与「告知」两义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses slide from a friendly opinion to paid expertise to a bare official notification.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从朋友式的意见，滑向付费的专业本领，再到纯粹的官方告知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old captain reading the wind and pointing to the safer channel.
core.cn: 核心意象：老船长看风，指向更安全的航道。

branches.en: a doctor sending a patient home to rest
branches.cn: 医生让病人回家休息

branches.en: a friend urging you against a risky deal
branches.cn: 朋友劝你不要碰一笔有风险的交易

branches.en: an expert paid to report on energy policy
branches.cn: 受聘就能源政策提出报告的专家

branches.en: a letter telling a client of a new address
branches.cn: 告知客户地址变更的信

branches.en: one act of putting a judgment in front of someone
branches.cn: 同一个动作：把判断摆到某人面前

definition_zh: 提倡者；拥护者；辩护律师；提倡、主张
definition_en: a person who publicly supports a cause, a lawyer who speaks for another, or the act of publicly recommending something
core_image: 法庭上紧挨被告站着的那个人，替他开口说话
scene: 社区会议上，居民们争论是否保留老图书馆。She advocated keeping the building open at weekends.
sceneCN: 这里的 advocate 是「提倡、主张」（第 3 个义项：公开支持某项做法）；句意是她主张周末继续开放这栋建筑。

pos.zh: 名词：提倡者；拥护者；辩护律师
动词：提倡；主张；拥护

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「拥护；倡导」
加 -or 构成，义为「拥护者」（较少用）
加 -ion 构成，义为「提倡的行为」（罕用）

senses.title: A public supporter of a cause
senses.definition: a person who publicly argues in favour of a policy, idea, or group
senses.definitionCN: 公开为某项政策、理念或群体辩护、争取的人
senses.example: She has long been an advocate of free school meals.
senses.exampleCN: 她长期以来一直是免费校餐的拥护者。
senses.why: Latin advocatus was one called to speak beside a person in court; the noun widened to anyone who speaks up for a cause.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 advocatus 指被叫到法庭上站在某人身边发言的人；名词后来扩大到任何为一个事业发声的人。

senses.title: A lawyer who speaks for another
senses.definition: a lawyer, especially in Scottish law, who presents a case in court for a client
senses.definitionCN: 尤指苏格兰法律中在法庭上替委托人陈述案情的律师
senses.example: The advocate rose to question the witness.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师起身询问证人。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense kept alive: the courtroom figure whose whole role is to speak on someone else's behalf.
senses.whyCN: 这是保存下来最古老的义项：法庭上那个全部职责就是替别人说话的角色。

senses.title: To argue publicly for something
senses.definition: to recommend or support a policy or action publicly and often repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 公开且常常反复地推荐或支持某项政策或行动
senses.example: She advocated keeping the building open at weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 她主张周末继续开放这栋建筑。
senses.why: The verb turns the courtroom role into an activity: anyone can now stand beside an idea and speak for it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个法庭角色变成一种活动：如今任何人都可以站到一个理念旁边替它说话。

intro.en: A Latin word for a voice called to one's side, still audible in the courtroom sense.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁词，本指被叫到身边来的声音，法庭义至今仍听得见这层本意。

items.en: vocare meant to call, and it gives vocation, vocal and vocabulary as well as this family.
items.cn: vocare 意为「呼叫」，它给出 vocation、vocal、vocabulary 以及这一族词。

items.en: ad 'to' plus vocare 'call' formed advocare, to call someone to one's aid, especially in a dispute.
items.cn: ad（向）加 vocare（呼叫）构成 advocare，意为「把某人叫来帮忙」，尤指争讼时。

items.en: The noun advocatus named the person called in to speak for another, the ancestor of the courtroom advocate.
items.cn: 名词 advocatus 指被叫来替别人发言的人，正是法庭上 advocate 的祖先。

items.en: Old French avocat carried the legal sense into English, where it named a lawyer pleading a case.
items.cn: 古法语 avocat 把法律义带入英语，指在庭上陈述案情的律师。

items.en: Since the eighteenth century the word has also worked as a verb meaning to speak publicly in favour of a cause.
items.cn: 十八世纪以后，这个词也作动词用，表示公开为一个事业发声。

note.en: The first group shares the calling root; the second gathers words for supporters and for speaking up.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「呼叫」的词根；第二组收表示「支持者」与「发声」的词。

entries.definition: public support for a cause or policy
one who advocates; a rare synonym of advocate
entries.definitionCN: 拥护者；较少见的同义词

entries.definition: a calling to a particular kind of work
a green fruit; only looks similar and comes from Nahuatl

entries.definition: someone who backs a person, team, or idea

to defend or support a cause actively

normalIntro.en: The word is built from vocare, to call: an advocate is called to someone's side.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 vocare「呼叫」构成：advocate 是被叫到某人身边的那位。

normal.en: ad- is to and vocare is to call, so an advocate is called to your side.
normal.cn: ad- 是「向」，vocare 是「呼叫」，advocate 就是被叫到你身边的人。

normal.en: The same root gives vocal, vocation and vocabulary.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 vocal、vocation 与 vocabulary。

normal.en: The noun stresses -cate, while the verb ends with a clear -ate sound.
normal.cn: 名词重音在前，动词结尾的 -ate 读得更清楚。

normal.en: An advocate of reform speaks for reform; the verb advocate reform does the same.
normal.cn: an advocate of reform 替改革说话；动词 advocate reform 做的是同一件事。

normal.en: A devil's advocate argues the other side just to test an idea.
normal.cn: devil's advocate 只为检验一个想法而故意站到对面。

abstract.en: Picture a figure standing shoulder to shoulder with the accused, speaking when the accused cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人与被告并肩而立，在被告说不出话时替他开口。

abstract.en: See the same stance outside court, beside a library or a policy rather than a person.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的姿态移到庭外，旁边不是人，而是一座图书馆或一项政策。

abstract.en: Imagine a voice called across a room simply to lend someone its strength.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音被叫过整个房间，只为把自己的力量借给某人。

examples.en: She has long been an advocate of free school meals.
examples.cn: 她长期以来一直是免费校餐的拥护者。

examples.en: The advocate for the defence asked for a short delay.
examples.cn: 辩方律师请求短暂延期。

examples.en: Several doctors advocated a ban on smoking in cars.
examples.cn: 几位医生主张禁止在车内吸烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德沃克特」——爱得我特地把他叫到身边，替我说句话。

root: 拉丁语 advocatus 由 ad-「向」与 vocare「呼叫」构成，本指被叫来替人发言者；经古法语 avocat 进入英语，先指辩护律师，后引申为「拥护者」与动词「提倡」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses keep one scene: someone called to stand beside another and speak for them, in court, for a cause, or as an act.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共守一个场景：被叫来站在别人身旁替他说话——在法庭上、为一个事业，或作为一个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing shoulder to shoulder with the accused, speaking for him.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人与被告并肩，替他开口。

branches.en: a campaigner speaking for free school meals
branches.cn: 为免费校餐发声的倡导者

branches.en: a Scottish lawyer questioning a witness
branches.cn: 询问证人的苏格兰辩护律师

branches.en: residents arguing to keep a library open
branches.cn: 居民主张保留图书馆开放

branches.en: the campaigner and the campaign are the same stance

branches.en: a voice called to the side of a person, a cause, or a proposal
branches.cn: 被叫到一个人、一个事业或一项提议旁边的声音

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin verb of calling, and English noun and verb endings.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀、一个表示「呼叫」的拉丁动词，加上英语的名词与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: vocare, advocare and advocatus are recorded Latin; avocat is the French stage.

definition_zh: 飞机（英式英语）；（纸或模型）飞机
definition_en: a powered aircraft with fixed wings, called an airplane in American English, or a small model or paper copy of one
core_image: 草地上停着一架白色小飞机，机翼在阳光下投出细长的影子
scene: 第一次坐飞机的男孩把脸贴在舷窗上，看地面一点点变小。The aeroplane climbed slowly above the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里的 aeroplane 是「飞机」（第 1 个义项：英式英语对固定翼航空器的称呼）；句意是飞机缓缓爬升到云层之上。

pos.zh: 名词：飞机（英式）；纸飞机；飞机模型

derivatives.zh: 美式拼写变体，义为「飞机」
由希腊语「空气」与「航行」两部分构成，义为「航空学」
由「空气」与「水手」两部分构成，义为「飞艇或气球驾驶员」
由「空气」与「跑道」两部分构成，义为「小型机场」

senses.title: A fixed-wing aircraft
senses.definition: a powered flying vehicle with fixed wings, the ordinary British word for an airplane
senses.definitionCN: 有固定机翼的动力飞行器，英式英语里的常用说法
senses.example: The aeroplane climbed slowly above the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机缓缓爬升到云层之上。
senses.why: The word joins Greek aer, air, to Greek planos, wandering: a craft that wanders through the air instead of staying on a fixed path.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊语 aer「空气」与 planos「游荡」合在一起：一种在空中游走、不守固定路线的机器。

senses.title: A model or paper copy
senses.definition: a small toy or folded paper object shaped like an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 做成飞机形状的小玩具或折纸物件
senses.example: He folded an aeroplane from a sheet of newspaper and threw it across the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一张报纸折了架飞机，把它扔过房间。
senses.why: Once the word names the shape rather than the machine, any small imitation of that shape can carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指的是那个形状而不是那台机器时，任何模仿该形状的小物件都能用这个名字。

intro.en: A French coinage from two Greek pieces, air and wandering.
intro.cn: 一个法语新造词，由「空气」与「游荡」两个希腊部件拼成。

items.en: aer meant the lower air, the misty layer near the earth, as opposed to the clear upper sky.
items.cn: aer 指靠近地面的雾气层，即下层空气，与高处的清澈天空相对。

items.en: planos meant wandering or roaming, from the verb planasthai, to stray about.
items.cn: planos 意为「游荡的、漫游的」，来自动词 planasthai「四处游走」。

items.en: French coined aéroplane in the mid nineteenth century for an aircraft with fixed wings.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪中期造出 aéroplane，指有固定机翼的飞行器。

items.en: English borrowed the French word and used it first for early experimental flying machines.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语词，最初用来指早期的实验飞行器。

items.en: British English keeps aeroplane, while American English settled on airplane after the Wright brothers' flights.
items.cn: 英式英语保留 aeroplane，美式英语则在莱特兄弟飞行之后定下 airplane。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek element for air; the second collects the everyday words for flying machines.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「空气」的希腊成分；第二组收日常说「飞行器」的几个词。

entries.definition: the American spelling and word for the same machine
entries.definitionCN: 同一机器的美式说法与拼写

entries.definition: the science of flight and aircraft design
a small airport, especially in British usage
a traveller in a balloon or airship
any vehicle that flies, including helicopters; broader than aeroplane
entries.definitionCN: 任何飞行器，包括直升机；范围比 aeroplane 宽

entries.definition: the short everyday word for an aeroplane
an aircraft driven by jet engines
an aircraft that flies without an engine

normalIntro.en: Two Greek pieces, air and wandering, plus the French ending that names a machine.
normalIntro.cn: 两个希腊部件「空气」与「游荡」，加上法语里指机器的词尾。

normal.en: aero- means air, and -plane here comes from a Greek word for wandering.
normal.cn: aero- 表示「空气」，这里的 -plane 来自希腊语「游荡」。

normal.en: British travellers say aeroplane; American travellers say airplane.
normal.cn: 英国旅客说 aeroplane，美国旅客说 airplane。

normal.en: A paper aeroplane keeps the shape but loses the engine.
normal.cn: 纸飞机保留了形状，却没有了发动机。

normal.en: The same aero- appears in aerodrome and aeronautics.
normal.cn: 同一个 aero- 也出现在 aerodrome 与 aeronautics 中。

normal.en: Spell it with aero-, not airo-.
normal.cn: 拼写用 aero-，不要写成 airo-。

abstract.en: Picture a white machine wandering through a grey sky like a fish through water.
abstract.cn: 想象一架白色机器像鱼游过水一样，在灰色天空里游走。

abstract.en: See a child's hand release a folded wing that wanders to the far wall.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子的手放开一只折出的翅膀，它一路游荡到远墙。

abstract.en: Imagine the same word shrinking from a machine to a toy and keeping its name.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词从机器缩成玩具，却仍留着原来的名字。

examples.en: The aeroplane from Paris landed ten minutes late.
examples.cn: 从巴黎飞来的飞机晚了十分钟降落。

examples.en: They crossed the mountains by aeroplane instead of by train.
examples.cn: 他们没有坐火车，而是乘飞机越过群山。

examples.en: A paper aeroplane sailed from the back row to the teacher's desk.
examples.cn: 一架纸飞机从后排滑到讲台上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱若普兰」——爱若飘在空气里，就折成一架飞机让它慢慢游。

root: 法语 aéroplane 由希腊语 aer「空气」与 planos「游荡的」构成，十九世纪中期造出，指固定翼飞行器；英语借入后成为英式常用词。

sensesIntro.en: One sense names the machine, the other names the shape; both go wandering through the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项指那台机器，另一个义项指那个形状；两者都在空中游走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white machine wandering through a grey sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架白色机器在灰色天空中游走。

branches.en: a plane climbing above the clouds
branches.cn: 爬升到云上的飞机

branches.en: a late flight from Paris
branches.cn: 从巴黎晚点到达的航班

branches.en: a folded paper wing crossing a classroom
branches.cn: 飞过教室的折纸翅膀

branches.en: a model hanging from a child's ceiling
branches.cn: 挂在孩子房间天花板上的模型

branches.en: the machine and its small imitation
branches.cn: 机器本身与它的小小仿制品

intro.en: A Greek word for air, a Greek word for wandering, and a French ending.
intro.cn: 一个希腊语的「空气」、一个希腊语的「游荡」，再加一个法语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, not Latin, so no Latin entries are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这些部件来自希腊语而非拉丁语，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 审美的；美学的；有审美情趣的；美学；审美观
definition_en: relating to beauty and the judgment of taste, pleasing in appearance, or the set of principles behind a style
core_image: 美术馆里，一个人退后两步，眯起眼打量整面墙的构图
scene: 展厅里灯光很暗，参观者却迟迟挪不动脚。The gallery's aesthetic appeal drew crowds even on weekdays.
sceneCN: 这里的 aesthetic 是「审美的」（第 1 个义项：与美感判断有关的）；句意是这家画廊的审美吸引力连工作日都能引来人群。

pos.zh: 形容词：审美的；美学的；悦目的
名词：美学；审美观

derivatives.zh: 加 -s 构成，义为「美学（学科）」
由同一希腊词根构成，义为「唯美主义者；审美家」
加 -ally 构成，义为「在审美上；从美学角度」
加 -ism 构成，义为「唯美主义」

senses.title: Relating to beauty and taste
senses.definition: concerned with beauty, art, and judgments of taste rather than with usefulness
senses.definitionCN: 关涉美、艺术与品味判断，而不是实用性的
senses.example: The building has real aesthetic value, even if it is costly to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼确有美学价值，尽管取暖费用很高。
senses.why: Greek aisthetikos meant 'of sense perception'; the word moved from what the senses take in to the special pleasure of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aisthetikos 意为「与感官知觉有关的」；这个词从感官接收之物，转到美感带来的特殊愉悦。

senses.title: Pleasing in appearance
senses.definition: attractive or well designed in a way that shows good taste
senses.definitionCN: 在外观上悦目，或设计体现出良好品味
senses.example: The new bridge is aesthetic as well as strong.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新桥既结实又美观。
senses.why: When the adjective describes a thing rather than a study, it means the thing satisfies the taste that the first sense names.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词形容一件东西而不是一门学问时，它指该物满足了第一义项所说的那种品味。

senses.title: A set of principles of style
senses.definition: the ideas about beauty and style that shape a work, a movement, or a person's taste
senses.definitionCN: 塑造一件作品、一个流派或一个人品味的关于美与风格的理念
senses.example: The film's aesthetic owes much to 1970s photography.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的审美风格很大程度上借鉴了七十年代的摄影。
senses.why: As a noun the word names not beauty itself but the system of ideas that decides what counts as beautiful.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词指的不是美本身，而是决定什么算美的那套理念系统。

intro.en: A Greek word about sense perception, made into a German science of beauty and then borrowed by English.
intro.cn: 一个关于感官知觉的希腊词，在德国被造成「美的学问」，随后被英语借走。

items.en: aisthesthai meant to perceive with the senses, to feel or notice something through the body.
items.cn: aisthesthai 意为用感官感知，通过身体去感觉或察觉。

items.en: aisthetikos meant 'of perception', concerned with what can be sensed rather than with pure thought.
items.cn: aisthetikos 意为「与知觉有关的」，关注可被感知之物，而非纯粹思想。

items.en: In the eighteenth century German writers made Aesthetik the name of a new discipline of beauty and art.
items.cn: 十八世纪德国作家把 Aesthetik 用作一门研究美与艺术的新学科之名。

items.en: English borrowed aesthetic from German, first as a term of philosophy and then of art criticism.
items.cn: 英语从德语借入 aesthetic，先作哲学术语，后进入艺术批评。

items.en: Everyday use now allows aesthetic to mean simply pleasing to look at, beyond its technical sense.
items.cn: 今天的日常用法让它超出专业范围，直接表示「看上去悦目」。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root of perception; the second gathers words about beauty and style.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「知觉」的希腊词根；第二组收关于美与风格的词。

entries.definition: the branch of philosophy that studies beauty
a person who cares greatly about beauty
in terms of beauty or appearance
a drug that removes feeling; same perception root, other prefix
entries.definitionCN: 麻醉剂；同词根但前缀不同，意思相反

entries.definition: relating to art or showing skill in art
showing good judgment in beauty and style
pleasing to the senses; more emotional than aesthetic
entries.definitionCN: 美丽的；比 aesthetic 更带情感

entries.definition: relating to the manner of expression rather than beauty
entries.definitionCN: 风格上的；侧重表达方式

normalIntro.en: The root means perception: aesthetic is about what the senses judge as beautiful.
normalIntro.cn: 词根意为「知觉」：aesthetic 讲的是感官判定为美的东西。

normal.en: The Greek root aisthet- means perceive, so aesthetic is about felt beauty.
normal.cn: 希腊词根 aisthet- 意为「感知」，所以 aesthetic 关乎被感受到的美。

normal.en: An anesthetic removes perception; an aesthetic sharpens it.
normal.cn: anesthetic 去掉知觉，aesthetic 则磨锐知觉。

normal.en: Use aesthetically to describe how something looks.
normal.cn: 用 aesthetically 来描述某物看上去如何。

normal.en: An aesthete is a person who lives for beauty.
normal.cn: an aesthete 是为美而活的人。

normal.en: Spell it with ae-, and keep the th before the final -etic.
normal.cn: 拼写以 ae- 开头，结尾 -etic 前要先写 th。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor stepping back from a wall of paintings to judge the whole arrangement.
abstract.cn: 想象参观者从一整墙画前退后两步，判断整体布局。

abstract.en: See the same judgment applied to a bridge, where strength and shape must agree.
abstract.cn: 想象同一种判断落到一座桥上，强度与形状必须彼此相称。

abstract.en: Imagine the rules behind the judgment written down as a system of taste.
abstract.cn: 想象把判断背后的规则写成一套品味体系。

examples.en: The old factory has little aesthetic value but great historical interest.
examples.cn: 这座旧工厂没什么美学价值，却有很高的历史意义。

examples.en: Her garden is practical rather than aesthetic.
examples.cn: 她的花园重实用胜过美观。

examples.en: The designer explained the film's aesthetic in a short interview.
examples.cn: 设计师在简短访谈中解释了这部电影的审美取向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊斯赛提克」——伊斯在美术馆里退后两步，赛着看谁的品味更高。

root: 希腊语 aisthetikos「与知觉有关的」来自 aisthesthai「感知」；十八世纪德语把它造成研究美的学科名，英语随后借入，兼指「审美的」「悦目的」与「审美观」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses move from the study of beauty, to a thing that satisfies it, to the system of taste behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从研究美的学问，走到满足这种学问的东西，再到它背后的品味体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visitor steps back to judge a whole wall of paintings.
core.cn: 核心意象：参观者退后两步，判断整墙画作。

branches.en: a listed building valued for beauty, not profit
branches.cn: 因美而非因盈利被珍视的登录建筑

branches.en: a question of taste rather than use
branches.cn: 关乎品味而非用途的问题

branches.en: a bridge whose shape pleases the eye
branches.cn: 外形悦目的桥

branches.en: a film borrowing the look of old photography
branches.cn: 借鉴旧摄影外观的电影

branches.en: perception, then pleasure, then the rules of pleasure
branches.cn: 先知觉，再愉悦，最后是愉悦的规则

intro.en: A Greek verb of perceiving, its adjective, and English endings.
intro.cn: 一个表示「感知」的希腊动词、它的形容词，加上英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek; Latin borrowed it only as a learned term, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语；拉丁语只把它当作学术借词使用，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

items.meaning: of beauty; a system of taste

definition_zh: 事情；事件；（复数）事务；风流韵事
definition_en: a matter or event, matters of business or public concern in the plural, or a secret romantic relationship
core_image: 书桌上一叠待办的文件，每一份都标着不同的名目
scene: 晚饭后，父亲把报纸摊开，皱着眉看国际版面。He followed foreign affairs long before he became a diplomat.
sceneCN: 这里的 affairs 是「事务」（第 2 个义项：复数形式指某一领域的事务）；句意是他早在成为外交官之前就关注国际事务。

pos.zh: 名词：事情；事件；事务；风流韵事

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「事务；业务」
同出拉丁语 facere「做」，义为「事实」
同出 facere，义为「结果；效果」

senses.title: A matter or event
senses.definition: a matter, situation, or event, often one that is being discussed or managed
senses.definitionCN: 一件被谈论或处理的事情、情形或事件
senses.example: The wedding was a quiet family affair.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼是一次安静的家庭活动。
senses.why: Old French afaire literally meant 'to do': an affair is simply something there is to do or to deal with.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 afaire 字面就是「去做」：affair 就是一件有待去做、有待处理的事。

senses.title: Matters of business or public concern
senses.definition: in the plural, the business, interests, or public matters of a person, company, or country
senses.definitionCN: 用复数时，指个人、公司或国家的业务、利益或公共事务
senses.example: She handles the company's legal affairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她负责处理公司的法律事务。
senses.why: A single matter is an affair, but a whole field of matters becomes affairs, the ordinary plural for business and government.
senses.whyCN: 单件事情是一个 affair，而一整个领域的事情就成了 affairs，这是商业与政务里的常规复数。

senses.title: A secret romantic relationship
senses.definition: a romantic or sexual relationship, especially one kept secret or outside marriage
senses.definitionCN: 浪漫或性的关系，尤指隐秘的或婚外的
senses.example: Their affair lasted only one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的恋情只维持了一个夏天。
senses.why: The neutral sense of 'a matter between two people' narrowed to the one matter people prefer to keep private.
senses.whyCN: 「两人之间的一件事」这个中性义，收窄成了人们最想保密的那件事。

intro.en: A French phrase meaning 'to do', worn down into a noun for anything there is to do.
intro.cn: 一个意为「去做」的法语短语，磨损成一个指「任何待办之事」的名词。

items.en: facere meant to do or make, and it gives fact, effect, factory and difficult as well as this word.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，它给出 fact、effect、factory、difficult 以及这个词。

items.en: The phrase ad faciendum, 'to be done', expressed work that lies ahead.
items.cn: 短语 ad faciendum 意为「有待去做」，指摆在面前的工作。

items.en: Old French contracted the phrase to a faire, 'to do', and used it for business or matters to attend to.
items.cn: 古法语把短语缩成 a faire「去做」，用来指事务或需要处理的事情。

items.en: Middle English borrowed afaire for a matter or business, then widened it to any event or concern.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 afaire 指「事情、事务」，后来扩大到任何事件或关切。

items.en: The plural affairs settled into politics and commerce, while the singular took on the romantic sense in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 复数 affairs 固定在政治与商业里，单数则在十八世纪发展出恋情义。

note.en: The first group looks alike but splits into different roots; the second gathers words for matters and relationships.
note.cn: 第一组拼写相近但词根不同；第二组收表示「事情」与「关系」的词。

entries.definition: to influence or move someone; built on facere, to do
entries.definitionCN: 影响；打动；同样出自 facere

entries.definition: a result or change produced by a cause
the plural used for business and public matters
entries.definitionCN: 复数，指业务与公共事务

entries.definition: friendly and easy to talk to; a different root from affair
entries.definitionCN: 和蔼可亲的；与 affair 词源不同

entries.definition: a subject or situation under discussion
work, trade, or matters that concern someone
something that happens, especially something notable
a love relationship, often idealised

normalIntro.en: The word is a worn-down French phrase for 'to do', so it names whatever is to be done.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是法语「去做」磨损而来，因此指一切待办之事。

normal.en: a faire in Old French meant to do, and an affair is a thing to do.
normal.cn: 古法语 a faire 意为「去做」，affair 就是一件要做的事。

normal.en: The plural affairs is the normal word for business and politics.
normal.cn: 复数 affairs 是商业与政治的常规说法。

normal.en: Keep the double f and the -air ending together: affair.
normal.cn: 记住双 f 与 -air 结尾连在一起：affair。

normal.en: A love affair is the private version of a public matter.
normal.cn: love affair 是公共事务的私人版本。

normal.en: The same Latin facere hides in fact, effect and factory.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁语 facere 藏在 fact、effect 与 factory 里。

abstract.en: Picture a desk covered with folders, each one a separate thing to be dealt with.
abstract.cn: 想象一张铺满文件夹的书桌，每一份都是一件待处理的事。

abstract.en: See one folder lifted out and marked private, then locked in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象其中一份被抽出，标上「私密」，锁进抽屉。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole wall of folders turning into a ministry's business.
abstract.cn: 想象一整墙文件夹变成一个部门的公务。

examples.en: The whole trip became a complicated affair.
examples.cn: 整趟旅行变成了一件麻烦事。

examples.en: She was appointed to manage the city's financial affairs.
examples.cn: 她被任命管理这座城市的财政事务。

examples.en: The novel describes a long affair between two neighbours.
examples.cn: 这部小说描写了两位邻居之间的一段长久恋情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费尔」——阿费尔桌上摊着一叠事，公事私事都算一件事。

root: 古法语 a faire「去做」来自拉丁语 facere「做」，进入英语作 affair，本指「待办之事」，复数 affairs 专指业务与公共事务，单数后又衍生出「恋情」义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one frame: something there is to do, whether a single event, a field of business, or a private relationship.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用同一个框架：一件有待处理之事，可以是单个事件、一片业务，或一段私人关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk covered with folders, each one a matter to handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：铺满文件夹的书桌，每份都是待办之事。

branches.en: a wedding kept small and quiet
branches.cn: 办得小而安静的一场婚礼

branches.en: a company's legal business
branches.cn: 公司的法律事务

branches.en: a diplomat reading the foreign pages
branches.cn: 外交官翻阅国际版面

branches.en: a summer relationship kept out of sight
branches.cn: 藏着的一段夏日恋情

branches.en: one 'thing to do', public or private
branches.cn: 同一件「要做的事」，或公或私

intro.en: A Latin verb of doing, worn down through French into a noun.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的拉丁动词，经法语磨损成一个名词。

latinIntro.en: facere is recorded Latin; a faire is the Old French contraction.
latinIntro.cn: facere 是有记录的拉丁词；a faire 是古法语的缩合形式。

definition_zh: 影响；感动；假装；患有（疾病）
definition_en: to produce a change in someone or something, to move the feelings, to pretend to feel something, or to be suffering from an illness
core_image: 一颗石子落进平静的水面，涟漪一圈圈推到岸边
scene: 坏消息传来时，会议室里没人说话。The news affected everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里的 affect 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对人或事物产生作用）；句意是这条消息影响了屋里的每个人。

pos.zh: 动词：影响；感动；假装；患有

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「喜爱；感情」
过去分词转作形容词，义为「受到影响的；做作的」
现在分词转作形容词，义为「动人的；令人感伤的」
加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「不满的；不忠的」

senses.title: To produce a change in something
senses.definition: to cause a change in a person, thing, or situation, often without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 使人、事物或情形发生变化，常非有意为之
senses.example: The news affected everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息影响了屋里的每个人。
senses.why: Latin afficere meant to do something to a thing; the English verb keeps that outward push of one thing upon another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 afficere 意为「对某物施加作用」；英语动词保留了这种一物推向另一物的外力。

senses.title: To move the feelings
senses.definition: to touch someone emotionally, often strongly
senses.definitionCN: 在情感上打动某人，程度常较深
senses.example: The letters from the children affected him more than he expected.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们的信比他预想的更让他感动。
senses.why: The same push can land on the feelings rather than on circumstances; what is affected is then the heart.
senses.whyCN: 同一种推力可以落在情感上而不是境况上；这时被作用的是人心。

senses.title: To pretend to have a feeling
senses.definition: to behave as if you have a quality or feeling that you do not really have
senses.definitionCN: 表现得好像拥有某种其实并不具备的品质或感受
senses.example: He affected indifference whenever her name was mentioned.
senses.exampleCN: 每当有人提到她的名字，他就装作不在意。
senses.why: A person can also push a false appearance outward on purpose, and the verb then names that controlled display.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以故意向外推出一个虚假的外表，这时动词指的就是这种受控的展示。

senses.title: To be suffering from an illness
senses.definition: to be attacked or troubled by a disease or condition, used mostly in passive forms
senses.definitionCN: 受到疾病或病症侵袭，多用于被动形式
senses.example: The cattle were affected with a disease of the joints.
senses.exampleCN: 这些牛患上了关节疾病。
senses.why: In medicine the outward push becomes an affliction: the body is acted upon by the disease, so the passive form is usual.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，这种外力变成病痛：身体被疾病施加作用，因此常用被动形式。

intro.en: A Latin verb of doing something to something, narrowed in English to influence and feeling.
intro.cn: 一个表示「对某物施加作用」的拉丁动词，在英语里收窄为「影响」与「情感」。

items.en: facere meant to do or make, the base of fact, effect, factory and this verb.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，是 fact、effect、factory 与这个动词的底子。

items.en: ad 'to' plus facere 'do' formed afficere, to do something to a person or thing, to act upon it.
items.cn: ad（向）加 facere（做）构成 afficere，意为对某人某物施加作用。

items.en: The participle affectus meant 'acted upon' and also named a state of mind or feeling.
items.cn: 分词 affectus 意为「被作用的」，也用来指心境或情感状态。

items.en: Old French affecter meant to desire, seek, or pretend, and gave English the 'pretend' sense.
items.cn: 古法语 affecter 意为「欲求、追求、假装」，给英语留下了「假装」这一义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps affect for influence and feeling, while effect became the noun for a result.
items.cn: 现代英语用 affect 表示影响与感动，而 effect 则成为表示「结果」的名词。

note.en: The first group is the confusing -fect family; the second gathers verbs of influence, feeling, and pretence.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的 -fect 词族；第二组收表示「影响、感动、假装」的动词。

entries.definition: a result; usually a noun, though it can be a verb meaning to bring about
entries.definitionCN: 结果；通常作名词，也可作动词表「实现」

normal.en: ad- plus facere gives 'do to', which becomes influence.
normal.cn: ad- 加 facere 得出「对……做」，于是有了「影响」。

normal.en: The feelings sense survives in affection and affecting.
normal.cn: 情感义还活在 affection 与 affecting 里。

normal.en: To affect an accent is to put on a false one.
normal.cn: affect an accent 就是装出一种假口音。

normal.en: In medical writing the passive be affected with is common.
normal.cn: 医学文本里常用被动的 be affected with。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped in still water, rings reaching the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进静水，涟漪一路推到岸边。

abstract.en: See the same rings arriving not at sand but at a listener's face.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的涟漪不是拍到沙上，而是拍到一个听者的脸上。

abstract.en: Imagine a man wearing a mask of calm while the rings still move beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人戴着平静的面具，面具下涟漪仍在动。

examples.en: Rising prices affect the poorest families most.
examples.cn: 物价上涨对最贫困的家庭影响最大。

examples.en: The story affected the whole audience.
examples.cn: 这个故事打动了全场观众。

examples.en: He affected a confidence he did not feel.
examples.cn: 他装出一副自己并不具备的自信。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses all describe one thing acting on another: circumstances, feelings, a false appearance, or a disease.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都在说一物作用于另一物：作用于境况、情感、外表，或身体。

branches.cn: 物价改变一个家庭能买什么

branches.cn: 盖在狂跳的心上的一张平静面孔

definition_zh: 喜爱；关爱；（心理学）情感
definition_en: a feeling of fondness or tender attachment, or in psychology, feeling as opposed to thought
core_image: 母亲把孩子画的第一张画小心收进抽屉，指尖在纸上停了一下
scene: 老照片摊在桌上，祖母一张张慢慢摩挲。She looked at the old photographs with great affection.
sceneCN: 这里的 affection 是「喜爱之情」（第 1 个义项：对人、事物温和深厚的爱意）；句意是她满怀深情地看着那些旧照片。

pos.zh: 名词：喜爱；关爱；情感

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ion 还原为动词，义为「影响；感动」
加 -ate 构成，义为「充满深情的；亲昵的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「深情地」
由动词过去分词转作形容词，义为「受影响的；做作的」

senses.title: A feeling of fondness
senses.definition: a gentle feeling of liking or caring for a person, animal, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对人、动物或事物温和的喜欢与关心
senses.example: She looked at the old photographs with great affection.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀深情地看着那些旧照片。
senses.why: Latin affectio named a state of being moved; when what moves you is a person, the state settles into fondness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 affectio 指「被触动」的状态；当触动你的是一个人时，这种状态就沉淀为喜爱。

senses.title: Feeling as a mental faculty
senses.definition: in psychology, the emotional side of mental life as distinct from cognition
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中与认知相对的心灵的情感方面
senses.example: The study separates affection from rational judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把情感与理性判断分开。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the Latin noun's neutral meaning: any state of being moved, without the warmth of the everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 这个专业义项保留了拉丁名词的中性含义：任何被触动的状态，不带日常用语的温度。

intro.en: A Latin noun for being moved, narrowed in English from any state of feeling to warm liking.
intro.cn: 一个表示「被触动」的拉丁名词，在英语里从任何情感状态收窄为温暖的喜爱。

items.en: facere meant to do or make, the base of fact, effect and the verb afficere.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，是 fact、effect 与动词 afficere 的底子。

items.en: ad 'to' plus facere 'do' formed afficere, to do something to a person, to move or affect them.
items.cn: ad（向）加 facere（做）构成 afficere，意为对某人施加作用、使其动情。

items.en: affectio named the state produced by such action, a disposition or feeling of the mind.
items.cn: affectio 指这种作用产生的状态，即心境或情感。

items.en: Old French affection carried the noun into English with the sense of a settled feeling towards someone.
items.cn: 古法语 affection 把这个名词带入英语，指对某人稳定的情感。

items.en: Everyday English narrowed the word to fondness, while psychology kept the neutral sense of feeling.
items.cn: 日常英语把这个词收窄为「喜爱」，心理学则保留了中性的「情感」义。

note.en: The first group is the affect family; the second gathers words for warm attachment.
note.cn: 第一组是 affect 词族；第二组收表示「温暖依恋」的词。

entries.definition: to influence or move someone
influenced, or unnatural and pretended
moving the feelings; touching
showing fondness openly
a gentle liking for someone or something
a much stronger feeling of deep attachment
entries.definitionCN: 爱；程度比 affection 更强

entries.definition: kindly feeling shown towards others
a bond of affection that ties one to another

normalIntro.en: The noun is affect plus -ion: the state of being moved by someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是 affect 加 -ion：被人触动的状态。

normal.en: affection is the noun built on the verb affect, plus -ion.
normal.cn: affection 是在动词 affect 上加 -ion 构成的名词。

normal.en: The common pattern is affection for a person or place.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 affection for 一个人或一个地方。

normal.en: Affectionate is the adjective for someone who shows affection easily.
normal.cn: affectionate 形容一个人很容易流露喜爱。

normal.en: In psychology, affection means feeling rather than thought.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，affection 指情感而非思维。

normal.en: Spell the ending -ction, like action and connection.
normal.cn: 词尾拼作 -ction，与 action、connection 一样。

abstract.en: Picture a hand smoothing a child's drawing before it goes into a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把孩子的画抚平，再收进抽屉。

abstract.en: See the same warmth become a laboratory term for any feeling at all.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的温度变成实验室里指一切情感的术语。

abstract.en: Imagine a bond thin as thread but strong enough to hold a memory.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细如线的纽带，却足以拉住一段记忆。

examples.en: He speaks of his old school with real affection.
examples.cn: 他说起母校时带着真切的感情。

examples.en: The child showed affection by holding her hand.
examples.cn: 孩子拉着她的手来表达亲昵。

examples.en: Psychologists often contrast affection with reasoning.
examples.cn: 心理学家常把情感与推理相对照。

root: 拉丁语 affectio「被触动的状态」来自 afficere（ad- 加 facere「做」，意为对……施加作用）；经古法语 affection 进入英语，日常义收窄为「喜爱」，心理学仍用其中性的「情感」义。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses keep the same state of being moved: everyday warmth towards someone, and the neutral technical name for feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都保留「被触动」这一状态：日常里对人的温暖，以及专业上对情感的中性称呼。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把孩子的画抚平收好。

branches.cn: 祖母摩挲旧照片

branches.cn: 孩子拉手表示亲昵

branches.cn: 同一种被触动，生活里温暖，科学里中性

definition_zh: 买得起；负担得起；提供、给予；承受得起（后果）
definition_en: to have enough money or resources for something, to provide or give something, or to be able to bear a cost or risk
core_image: 橱窗里的价签旁，一只手在口袋里反复掂量硬币
scene: 学费通知单放在桌上，家里沉默了很久。They could not afford to move to a bigger flat.
sceneCN: 这里的 afford 是「负担得起」（第 1 个义项：有钱或有余力做某事）；句意是他们负担不起搬到更大的公寓。

pos.zh: 动词：买得起；负担得起；提供；承受得起

derivatives.zh: 加 -able 构成，义为「负担得起的；价格合理的」
由 affordable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可负担性」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「负担不起的」

senses.title: To have enough money for
senses.definition: to have enough money, time, or resources to pay for something or to do something
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够的钱、时间或资源来支付某物或做某事
senses.example: They could not afford to move to a bigger flat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们负担不起搬到更大的公寓。
senses.why: Old English forthian meant to further or carry out; to afford was to be able to carry the cost through.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 forthian 意为「推进、办成」；afford 就是有能力把这笔开销撑下来。

senses.title: To provide or give
senses.definition: to supply something valuable such as an opportunity, protection, or a view
senses.definitionCN: 提供机会、保护或视野等有价值之物
senses.example: The high wall affords some protection from the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵高墙提供了一些挡风的作用。
senses.why: If you can carry a cost, you can also extend a benefit outward; the verb then means to make something available to others.
senses.whyCN: 既然能撑起一笔开销，也就能把好处向外递出去；于是这个动词转为「使他人得到某物」。

senses.title: To be able to bear a risk
senses.definition: to be able to accept the cost or consequence of an action without being ruined
senses.definitionCN: 能够承受某个行动的代价或后果而不至于垮掉
senses.example: We cannot afford to ignore this warning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们承受不起忽视这个警告的后果。
senses.why: The cost here is not money but consequence; the same question 'can you carry it' is asked about risk.
senses.whyCN: 这里的代价不是钱而是后果；问的还是同一句「你撑得住吗」，只是对象换成了风险。

intro.en: An Old English verb of carrying something through, later narrowed to money and means.
intro.cn: 一个古英语动词，本指把事情办成、撑下来，后来收窄到金钱与能力。

items.en: forthian meant to further, promote, or carry out something.
items.cn: forthian 意为推进、促成或办成某事。

items.en: The prefixed form geforthian meant to accomplish or provide what is needed.
items.cn: 带前缀的形式 geforthian 意为完成或提供所需之物。

items.en: Middle English aforthen kept the sense of being able to manage or supply something.
items.cn: 中古英语 aforthen 保留了「有能力应付或供给」的意思。

items.en: By the fifteenth century afford commonly meant to have the means for something.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，afford 常指「有做某事的手段或财力」。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb from money to time, risk, and abstract benefits such as protection.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个动词从金钱扩展到时间、风险，以及保护之类的抽象好处。

note.en: The first group is built directly on afford; the second gathers verbs of paying, providing, and bearing.
note.cn: 第一组直接由 afford 构成；第二组收表示「支付、提供、承受」的动词。

normalIntro.en: The old verb meant to carry something through; money and risk are the loads it now carries.

normal.en: can afford is the usual frame; the negative cannot afford is even commoner.
normal.cn: 常见句框是 can afford，否定式 cannot afford 更常用。

normal.en: afford to do something means you have the means to do it.
normal.cn: afford to do something 就是有做它的条件。

normal.en: The wall affords protection uses the 'provide' sense.
normal.cn: the wall affords protection 用的是「提供」义。

normal.en: Affordable housing is housing people can pay for.
normal.cn: affordable housing 是人们付得起的住房。

normal.en: Spell it with a double f but a single r: afford.
normal.cn: 拼写是双 f、单 r：afford。

abstract.en: Picture a hand weighing coins beside a price tag it cannot meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在价签旁掂量硬币，却怎么也不够。

abstract.en: See a high wall turning the wind away from a small garden.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵高墙替小花园挡开风。

abstract.en: Imagine a warning placed on a table, and someone asking whether the family can carry it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张警告摆在桌上，有人问这家人是否扛得住。

examples.en: We cannot afford a new car this year.
examples.cn: 今年我们买不起新车。

examples.en: The terrace affords a fine view of the bay.
examples.cn: 这个露台能看到海湾的好景色。

examples.en: The team cannot afford another defeat.
examples.cn: 这支队伍承受不起再输一场。

definition_en: feeling fear about danger, worried about a possible bad result, or used politely to announce bad news
core_image: 孩子躲在门后，只露出一只眼睛看客厅里的陌生人
scene: 雷声在屋顶滚过，小狗钻到沙发底下。The dog is afraid of thunder.
sceneCN: 这里的 afraid 是「害怕的」（第 1 个义项：对危险或威胁感到恐惧）；句意是这只狗怕打雷。

pos.zh: 形容词：害怕的；担心的；恐怕（委婉表达）

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「恐惧；害怕」

senses.title: Feeling fear of danger
senses.definition: feeling fear because of a person, animal, thing, or situation that seems dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人、动物、事物或情形看似危险而感到恐惧
senses.example: The dog is afraid of thunder.
senses.exampleCN: 这只狗怕打雷。
senses.why: The word began as a past participle meaning 'frightened', so it still describes a person who has been scared rather than one who scares.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是意为「被吓到的」过去分词，因此它描述的始终是被吓到的人，而不是吓人的人。

senses.title: Worried about a result
senses.definition: worried that something bad may happen or may be true
senses.definitionCN: 担心某件坏事可能发生或可能属实
senses.example: She was afraid that the letter had been lost.
senses.exampleCN: 她担心那封信已经丢了。
senses.why: Fear can point forward to an outcome that has not happened yet; the word then means anxious rather than terrified.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧也可以指向尚未发生的结果；这时这个词表示焦虑，而不是惊恐。

senses.title: Polite regret: I'm afraid
senses.definition: used in the phrase I'm afraid to soften bad news or a refusal
senses.definitionCN: 用于 I'm afraid 这一短语，用来缓和坏消息或拒绝
senses.example: I'm afraid the last train has already gone.
senses.exampleCN: 恐怕末班车已经开走了。
senses.why: The speaker borrows a little fear to excuse the unwelcome news, turning a blunt statement into a polite one.
senses.whyCN: 说话者借来一点点「怕」，为不受欢迎的消息作缓冲，把直白的话变成客气的话。

intro.en: A French past participle meaning 'frightened', which English made into a predicative adjective.
intro.cn: 一个意为「被吓到的」法语过去分词，英语把它变成了只作表语的形容词。

items.en: The noun esfree meant fear or fright, and it sits behind the whole English family.
items.cn: 名词 esfree 意为「恐惧、惊吓」，是英语这一族词的源头。

items.en: The verb esfreer meant to frighten or alarm someone.
items.cn: 动词 esfreer 意为「使害怕、使惊恐」。

items.en: Its participle esfreit, later affine, described a person who had been frightened.
items.cn: 它的分词 esfreit（后来作 affine）描述一个被吓到的人。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the participle as affraid and used it only after verbs such as be and seem.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个分词借作 affraid，只放在 be、seem 这类动词之后。

items.en: The spelling settled as afraid, and the word never gained an attributive use before a noun.
items.cn: 拼写定为 afraid，而且这个词始终没有发展出放在名词前的定语用法。

note.en: The first group shares the French fear root; the second gathers adjectives of fear and worry.
note.cn: 第一组共享法语「恐惧」词根；第二组收表示「害怕、担忧」的形容词。

entries.definition: the noun and verb for the feeling of danger
feeling fear, or causing fear
without fear; brave
a public fight or disturbance; a legal word from the same French source
entries.definitionCN: 斗殴；扰乱治安；同出法语的法律用词

entries.definition: frightened; the everyday spoken word
suddenly made afraid by something
anxious about a possible problem
extremely afraid

normalIntro.en: Afraid is a worn French participle, so it only ever describes the one who feels fear.
normalIntro.cn: afraid 是磨损后的法语分词，因此永远只描述感到恐惧的那一方。

normal.en: Use afraid only after be, feel, or seem, never before a noun.
normal.cn: afraid 只放在 be、feel、seem 之后，不能放在名词前。

normal.en: afraid of a thing, afraid to do an action, afraid that a fact may be true.
normal.cn: afraid of 接事物，afraid to 接动作，afraid that 接可能属实的事。

normal.en: I'm afraid is the polite way to announce bad news.
normal.cn: I'm afraid 是告知坏消息时的客气说法。

normal.en: The word is related to fear but not built from it in English.
normal.cn: 这个词与 fear 同源，却不是英语里由 fear 构成的。

normal.en: Spell it with one f in the middle and -aid at the end.
normal.cn: 拼写中间一个 f，结尾是 -aid。

abstract.en: Picture a child behind a door, one eye showing.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子躲在门后，只露出一只眼睛。

abstract.en: See the same child waiting for a letter that may never come.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个孩子在等一封也许永远不来的信。

abstract.en: Imagine an official softening a refusal with a small borrowed fear.
abstract.cn: 想象一位职员借来一点「怕」，把拒绝说得柔和些。

examples.en: The dog is afraid of thunder.
examples.cn: 这只狗怕打雷。

examples.en: She was afraid that the letter had been lost.
